title: STCW hours of rest: the 10, 77, 6 and 14 hour rules explained
description: The minimum hours of rest under STCW and the Maritime Labour Convention: 10 hours in any 24 hours, 77 hours in any seven days, no more than two rest periods with one of at least 6 hours, and no more than 14 hours between rest periods. Why honest rest-hour records matter.

source.title: STCW Hours of Rest (policy letter quoting STCW regulation VIII/1 and section A-VIII/1)
C2.3.b. What are the standards for minimum hours of rest and maximum hours of work?

script: Fatigue is a safety hazard, so international rules set your minimum rest. Four numbers: ten, seventy-seven, six and fourteen. Under STCW and the Maritime Labour Convention, you must get at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period, and at least 77 hours in any seven-day period. Rest may be split into no more than two periods, and one of them must be at least 6 hours long. The gap between rest periods must not exceed 14 hours. Drills should disturb rest as little as possible. Your daily rest hours are recorded on board, and you get a copy. Record the truth: false records hide fatigue. Remember: ten in twenty-four, seventy-seven in seven. Follow HeyMariner for practical maritime knowledge.
